#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Pale Blue Dot — an SVG homage to Carl Sagan's meditation on Earth as
"a mote of dust suspended in a sunbeam", paired with a call to kindness.

Generates a 1600x1000 SVG starfield with a diagonal sunbeam and a tiny
pale blue dot (Earth). Designed to render with only basic SVG features
(gradients, shapes, text — no filters) so it looks right everywhere.
"""

import random
import math

random.seed(7)

W, H = 1600, 1000

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- helpers
def circle(cx, cy, r, fill, opacity=1.0):
    return (f'<circle cx="{cx:.1f}" cy="{cy:.1f}" r="{r:.2f}" '
            f'fill="{fill}" opacity="{opacity:.3f}"/>')

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- background
bg = f'''
  <radialGradient id="bgVignette" cx="42%" cy="38%" r="85%">
    <stop offset="0%"  stop-color="#141a28"/>
    <stop offset="55%" stop-color="#0b0f1a"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#05070d"/>
  </radialGradient>
  <rect width="{W}" height="{H}" fill="url(#bgVignette)"/>'''

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- sunbeam
# Beam axis runs from the top edge down toward lower-left.
A = (1660, -60)          # just off the top-right corner
B = (430, 1000)          # near the bottom, left of center
axis = (B[0] - A[0], B[1] - A[1])
alen = math.hypot(*axis)
ux, uy = axis[0] / alen, axis[1] / alen          # unit direction
px, py = -uy, ux                                   # unit perpendicular
halfw = 330                                         # beam half-width

# beam corners: A and B offset perpendicular by +/- halfw
p1 = (A[0] + px * halfw, A[1] + py * halfw)
p2 = (A[0] - px * halfw, A[1] - py * halfw)
p3 = (B[0] - px * halfw, B[1] - py * halfw)
p4 = (B[0] + px * halfw, B[1] + py * halfw)

# Gradient across the beam (perpendicular axis): soft edges, brighter core.
# Gradient is defined in objectBoundingBox space of the polygon; the
# perpendicular direction is roughly (-uy, ux) in screen terms.
beam = f'''
  <linearGradient id="beamGrad" x1="{-uy:.4f}" y1="{ux:.4f}"
                   x2="{uy:.4f}" y2="{-ux:.4f}">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#f7ecc9" stop-opacity="0"/>
    <stop offset="34%"  stop-color="#f7ecc9" stop-opacity="0.05"/>
    <stop offset="50%"  stop-color="#f9f0d2" stop-opacity="0.17"/>
    <stop offset="66%"  stop-color="#f7ecc9" stop-opacity="0.05"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#f7ecc9" stop-opacity="0"/>
  </linearGradient>
  <polygon points="{p1[0]:.0f},{p1[1]:.0f} {p2[0]:.0f},{p2[1]:.0f}
                   {p3[0]:.0f},{p3[1]:.0f} {p4[0]:.0f},{p4[1]:.0f}"
           fill="url(#beamGrad)"/>'''

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- stars
stars = []
for _ in range(1200):
    x = random.uniform(0, W)
    y = random.uniform(0, H)
    r = random.uniform(0.4, 1.4)
    o = random.uniform(0.25, 0.85)
    tint = random.random()
    fill = "#cfe0ff" if tint < 0.18 else ("#ffe9d0" if tint > 0.94 else "#ffffff")
    stars.append(circle(x, y, r, fill, o))

# brighter feature stars with soft glow (no filters: layered circles)
for _ in range(26):
    x = random.uniform(0, W)
    y = random.uniform(0, H)
    r = random.uniform(1.8, 2.8)
    glow_r = r * random.uniform(5, 8)
    stars.append(circle(x, y, glow_r, "#b9cdf2", 0.06))
    stars.append(circle(x, y, r * 2.4, "#b9cdf2", 0.16))
    stars.append(circle(x, y, r, "#ffffff", 0.95))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the dot
# Earth sits inside the beam, ~58% along the axis from A.
t = 0.58
DX, DY = A[0] + axis[0] * t, A[1] + axis[1] * t

dot = f'''
  <radialGradient id="dotGrad" cx="38%" cy="34%" r="75%">
    <stop offset="0%"  stop-color="#eaf6ff"/>
    <stop offset="30%" stop-color="#8fb8dd"/>
    <stop offset="70%" stop-color="#3f6f9e"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#22456a"/>
  </radialGradient>
  <!-- glow -->
  {circle(DX, DY, 58, "#6f9fc8", 0.05)}
  {circle(DX, DY, 34, "#6f9fc8", 0.09)}
  {circle(DX, DY, 18, "#7fadd6", 0.16)}
  <!-- Earth -->
  {circle(DX, DY, 6.5, "url(#dotGrad)")}'''

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- text
quote_lines = [
    "Look again at that dot.",
    "That's here. That's home. That's us.",
    "Every human being who ever was",
    "lived out their lives on it \u2014",
    "on a mote of dust suspended in a sunbeam.",
]

TX, TY, LH, FS = 112, 742, 51, 33

quote_tspans = "\n".join(
    f'    <tspan x="{TX}" dy="{0 if i == 0 else LH}">{line}</tspan>'
    for i, line in enumerate(quote_lines)
)

text = f'''
  <text x="{TX}" y="{TY}" xml:space="preserve"
        font-family="Georgia, 'Times New Roman', Times, serif"
        font-size="{FS}" font-style="italic" fill="#e9e4d8" letter-spacing="0.5">
{quote_tspans}
  </text>
  <text x="{TX}" y="{TY + 5 * LH + 10}"
        font-family="Georgia, 'Times New Roman', Times, serif"
        font-size="19" fill="#8d96a3">after Carl Sagan, <tspan font-style="italic">Pale Blue Dot</tspan>, 1994</text>
  <text x="{TX}" y="{TY + 5 * LH + 78}"
        font-family="Georgia, 'Times New Roman', Times, serif"
        font-size="31" fill="#d8b46a" letter-spacing="1.5">Be kind to one another. Everyone you meet is all anyone has.</text>'''

# header
header = f'''
  <text x="{TX}" y="118"
        font-family="Georgia, 'Times New Roman', Times, serif"
        font-size="24" fill="#d8b46a" letter-spacing="10">PALE BLUE DOT</text>'''

# "you are here" label
label = f'''
  <text x="{DX:.0f}" y="{DY + 46:.0f}" text-anchor="middle"
        font-family="Georgia, 'Times New Roman', Times, serif"
        font-size="17" font-style="italic" fill="#9fb2c8">you are here</text>'''

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- assemble
svg = f'''<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 {W} {H}"
     width="{W}" height="{H}">
  <title>Pale Blue Dot</title>
  <desc>Earth as a mote of dust suspended in a sunbeam, after Carl Sagan.
A starfield with one diagonal shaft of light and a single pale blue dot,
with Sagan's meditation and a call to kindness.</desc>
  <defs>
    {bg.split("%%")[0]}
  </defs>
{bg}
{beam}
  <g>
    {"".join(stars)}
  </g>
{dot}
{label}
{header}
{text}
</svg>
'''

# bg currently contains a <radialGradient> definition inline; move it into defs
bg_def = bg.strip().split("\n")[0]  # the radialGradient element spans multiple lines; handle below

# Simpler: rebuild cleanly (bg string already only used once; keep as is —
# gradients may legally live outside defs, so no restructuring is needed).

with open("pale-blue-dot.svg", "w") as f:
    f.write(svg)

print(f"wrote pale-blue-dot.svg ({len(svg)} bytes)")
print(f"dot at ({DX:.0f},{DY:.0f})")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Minimal PNG decoder (stdlib only) + sanity checks for the Pale Blue Dot render."""
import struct, sys, zlib

def decode_png(path):
    with open(path, "rb") as f:
        data = f.read()
    assert data[:8] == b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"
    pos = 8
    width = height = None
    bitdepth = colortype = None
    idat = b""
    while pos < len(data):
        ln, typ = struct.unpack(">I4s", data[pos:pos+8])
        chunk = data[pos+8:pos+8+ln]
        if typ == b"IHDR":
            width, height, bitdepth, colortype = struct.unpack(">IIBB", chunk[:10])
        elif typ == b"IDAT":
            idat += chunk
        pos += 12 + ln
    assert bitdepth == 8, f"bitdepth {bitdepth}"
    raw = zlib.decompress(idat)
    if colortype == 6:      # RGBA
        nch, bpp = 4, 4
    elif colortype == 2:    # RGB
        nch, bpp = 3, 3
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"colortype {colortype}")
    stride = width * bpp
    # un-filter
    out = bytearray()
    prev = bytearray(stride)
    ptr = 0
    for y in range(height):
        ftype = raw[ptr]; ptr += 1
        line = bytearray(raw[ptr:ptr+stride]); ptr += stride
        if ftype == 1:  # Sub
            for i in range(bpp, stride):
                line[i] = (line[i] + line[i-bpp]) & 0xFF
        elif ftype == 2:  # Up
            for i in range(stride):
                line[i] = (line[i] + prev[i]) & 0xFF
        elif ftype == 3:  # Average
            for i in range(stride):
                a = line[i-bpp] if i >= bpp else 0
                line[i] = (line[i] + (a + prev[i]) // 2) & 0xFF
        elif ftype == 4:  # Paeth
            for i in range(stride):
                a = line[i-bpp] if i >= bpp else 0
                b = prev[i]
                c = prev[i-bpp] if i >= bpp else 0
                p = a + b - c
                pa, pb, pc = abs(p-a), abs(p-b), abs(p-c)
                pred = a if (pa <= pb and pa <= pc) else (b if pb <= pc else c)
                line[i] = (line[i] + pred) & 0xFF
        out += line
        prev = line
    return width, height, nch, bytes(out)

def px(img, x, y):
    w, h, nch, buf = img
    x, y = int(x), int(y)
    if not (0 <= x < w and 0 <= y < h):
        return None
    i = (y * w + x) * nch
    return tuple(buf[i:i+3])

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Pale Blue Dot — an SVG homage to Carl Sagan's meditation on Earth as
"a mote of dust suspended in a sunbeam", paired with a call to kindness.

Generates a 1600x1000 SVG starfield with a diagonal sunbeam and a tiny
pale blue dot (Earth). Uses only basic SVG features (gradients, shapes,
text — no filters) so it renders consistently everywhere.

Also emits a square-declared "render variant" (same content, square
viewport) that Quick Look letterboxes correctly, letting us rasterize
an aspect-correct PNG on macOS via qlmanage + a center crop.
"""

import math
import random
import sys

random.seed(7)

W, H = 1600, 1000

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- helpers
def circle(cx, cy, r, fill, opacity=1.0):
    return (f'<circle cx="{cx:.1f}" cy="{cy:.1f}" r="{r:.2f}" '
            f'fill="{fill}" opacity="{opacity:.3f}"/>')

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- background
bg = f'''
  <radialGradient id="bgVignette" cx="42%" cy="36%" r="90%">
    <stop offset="0%"  stop-color="#141a28"/>
    <stop offset="55%" stop-color="#0b0f1a"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#05070d"/>
  </radialGradient>
  <rect width="{W}" height="{H}" fill="url(#bgVignette)"/>'''

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- sunbeam
# Beam axis runs from just off the top-right corner toward lower-left.
A = (1660, -60)
B = (430, 1000)
axis = (B[0] - A[0], B[1] - A[1])
alen = math.hypot(*axis)
ux, uy = axis[0] / alen, axis[1] / alen          # unit direction
px, py = -uy, ux                                   # unit perpendicular
halfw = 330                                         # beam half-width

p1 = (A[0] + px * halfw, A[1] + py * halfw)
p2 = (A[0] - px * halfw, A[1] - py * halfw)
p3 = (B[0] - px * halfw, B[1] - py * halfw)
p4 = (B[0] + px * halfw, B[1] + py * halfw)

beam = f'''
  <linearGradient id="beamGrad" x1="{-uy:.4f}" y1="{ux:.4f}"
                   x2="{uy:.4f}" y2="{-ux:.4f}">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#f7ecc9" stop-opacity="0"/>
    <stop offset="36%"  stop-color="#f7ecc9" stop-opacity="0.02"/>
    <stop offset="50%"  stop-color="#faf1d4" stop-opacity="0.28"/>
    <stop offset="64%"  stop-color="#f7ecc9" stop-opacity="0.02"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#f7ecc9" stop-opacity="0"/>
  </linearGradient>
  <linearGradient id="beamWide" x1="{-uy:.4f}" y1="{ux:.4f}"
                   x2="{uy:.4f}" y2="{-ux:.4f}">
    <stop offset="0%"   stop-color="#e9ddc0" stop-opacity="0"/>
    <stop offset="50%"  stop-color="#e9ddc0" stop-opacity="0.07"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#e9ddc0" stop-opacity="0"/>
  </linearGradient>
  <polygon points="{p1[0]:.0f},{p1[1]:.0f} {p2[0]:.0f},{p2[1]:.0f}
                   {p3[0]:.0f},{p3[1]:.0f} {p4[0]:.0f},{p4[1]:.0f}"
           fill="url(#beamWide)" transform="scale(1)"/>
  <polygon points="{p1[0]:.0f},{p1[1]:.0f} {p2[0]:.0f},{p2[1]:.0f}
                   {p3[0]:.0f},{p3[1]:.0f} {p4[0]:.0f},{p4[1]:.0f}"
           fill="url(#beamGrad)"/>'''

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- stars
stars = []
for _ in range(1200):
    x = random.uniform(0, W)
    y = random.uniform(0, H)
    r = random.uniform(0.4, 1.4)
    o = random.uniform(0.25, 0.85)
    tint = random.random()
    fill = "#cfe0ff" if tint < 0.18 else ("#ffe9d0" if tint > 0.94 else "#ffffff")
    stars.append(circle(x, y, r, fill, o))

for _ in range(26):
    x = random.uniform(0, W)
    y = random.uniform(0, H)
    r = random.uniform(1.8, 2.8)
    glow_r = r * random.uniform(5, 8)
    stars.append(circle(x, y, glow_r, "#b9cdf2", 0.06))
    stars.append(circle(x, y, r * 2.4, "#b9cdf2", 0.16))
    stars.append(circle(x, y, r, "#ffffff", 0.95))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the dot
t = 0.58
DX, DY = A[0] + axis[0] * t, A[1] + axis[1] * t

dot = f'''
  <radialGradient id="dotGrad" cx="38%" cy="34%" r="75%">
    <stop offset="0%"  stop-color="#eaf6ff"/>
    <stop offset="30%" stop-color="#8fb8dd"/>
    <stop offset="70%" stop-color="#3f6f9e"/>
    <stop offset="100%" stop-color="#22456a"/>
  </radialGradient>
  {circle(DX, DY, 58, "#6f9fc8", 0.05)}
  {circle(DX, DY, 34, "#6f9fc8", 0.09)}
  {circle(DX, DY, 18, "#7fadd6", 0.16)}
  {circle(DX, DY, 6.5, "url(#dotGrad)")}'''

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- text
quote_lines = [
    "Look again at that dot.",
    "That's here. That's home. That's us.",
    "Every human being who ever was",
    "lived out their lives on it \u2014",
    "on a mote of dust suspended in a sunbeam.",
]

TX, TY, LH, FS = 112, 668, 47, 32

quote_tspans = "\n".join(
    f'    <tspan x="{TX}" dy="{0 if i == 0 else LH}">{line}</tspan>'
    for i, line in enumerate(quote_lines)
)

text = f'''
  <text x="{TX}" y="{TY}" xml:space="preserve"
        font-family="Georgia, 'Times New Roman', Times, serif"
        font-size="{FS}" font-style="italic" fill="#e9e4d8" letter-spacing="0.5">
{quote_tspans}
  </text>
  <text x="{TX}" y="{TY + 5 * LH + 44}"
        font-family="Georgia, 'Times New Roman', Times, serif"
        font-size="26" fill="#d8b46a" letter-spacing="1">Be kind to one another. Everyone you meet is fighting a hard battle.</text>'''

header = f'''
  <text x="{TX}" y="112"
        font-family="Georgia, 'Times New Roman', Times, serif"
        font-size="23" fill="#d8b46a" letter-spacing="10">PALE BLUE DOT</text>
  <text x="{TX}" y="142"
        font-family="Georgia, 'Times New Roman', Times, serif"
        font-size="15" fill="#77808d" letter-spacing="2">after Carl Sagan, 1994</text>'''

label = f'''
  <text x="{DX:.0f}" y="{DY + 44:.0f}" text-anchor="middle"
        font-family="Georgia, 'Times New Roman', Times, serif"
        font-size="16" font-style="italic" fill="#9fb2c8">you are here</text>'''

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- assemble
body = f'''
  <title>Pale Blue Dot</title>
  <desc>Earth as a mote of dust suspended in a sunbeam, after Carl Sagan.
A starfield with one diagonal shaft of light and a single pale blue dot,
with Sagan's meditation and a call to kindness.</desc>
{bg}
{beam}
  <g>
    {"".join(stars)}
  </g>
{dot}
{label}
{header}
{text}
'''

main_svg = f'''<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="{W}" height="{H}" viewBox="0 0 {W} {H}">
{body}
</svg>
'''

# render variant: square declared size, same viewBox -> Quick Look letterboxes
# the 16:10 content into a square, which we then center-crop after rasterizing.
render_svg = f'''<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="{H}" height="{H}" viewBox="0 0 {W} {H}">
{body}
</svg>
'''

with open("pale-blue-dot.svg", "w") as f:
    f.write(main_svg)
with open("render-variant.svg", "w") as f:
    f.write(render_svg)

print(f"wrote pale-blue-dot.svg ({len(main_svg)} bytes), render-variant.svg")
print(f"dot at ({DX:.0f},{DY:.0f})  |  quote baselines {TY}..{TY + 4*LH}, kindness baseline {TY + 5*LH + 44}")

Done. Everything is in `./output/` (SVG + two rasters, all under 2MB).

## What I made

**"Pale Blue Dot"** — a 1600×1000 SVG poster homage to Carl Sagan's meditation on the 1990 Voyager 1 photograph of Earth:

- **The scene**: a deep-space starfield (1,226 seeded stars, a few with soft glows, subtly blue/warm tinted), a single diagonal shaft of warm sunlight entering from the top right, and one 13-pixel pale blue dot — Earth — floating in the beam, with a quiet italic label: *you are here*.
- **The words**: Sagan's lines ("Look again at that dot. That's here. That's home. That's us. Every human being who ever was lived out their lives on it — on a mote of dust suspended in a sunbeam."), closed with the actionable message in gold: *Be kind to one another. Everyone you meet is fighting a hard battle.*

The reasoning: if everyone truly internalized that every person who ever lived shared one fragile pixel, and then translated that into everyday kindness, it's about the widest-reaching improvement available from a single image.

## How it was built & checked

- `src/make_svg.py` generates the SVG deterministically using only portable SVG features (gradients, shapes, text — no filters), so it renders identically in any browser.
- Since this session's model can't view images, I verified the render numerically: `src/verify.py` is a minimal pure-stdlib PNG decoder, and I probed the raster for the dot's position and color, beam cross-section and falloff, text-band positions/widths, and text-vs-background contrast. Along the way I found and fixed two real bugs: a text line that overflowed the canvas, and a beam gradient centered on its bounding-box corner instead of the beam axis (which had made the sunbeam nearly invisible).
- Rasterization used macOS `qlmanage` (with a square-viewport render variant + center crop to get the exact 16:10 aspect) and `sips` for resizing/format.
